verdicts.decision_note: The client defines the PCB mounting orientation, accessible connector edges, aligned interboard connector pairs, and short straight cable routing.
The client adds an implementation-relevant PCB layout rule minimizing connectors on the inaccessible downward-facing edges.
The client permits smaller connectors on side edges while retaining top-edge accessibility and identifies the layout as applying to the prototype phase.
The client specifies straight connectors pointing away from the PCB instead of right-angle connectors for the lower main-board positions.
The client adds a feasible-layout preference to relocate lower main-board connectors beneath the upper row in the same accessible orientation.
The client applies the upward relocation and top-down-access layout rule to the corresponding sensor-board connectors.

The source proposes a separate integrated-board project and milestone; it does not yet change the established layout state of the legacy three-board design, and assigning the legacy Requirement an integrated-board scope is incorrect.
The client confirms that the current single-board architecture eliminates interboard cables and therefore removes the legacy main-to-sensor connector-alignment requirement.
